note: Thresholds are the PRD's placeholders; every condition is mechanical. Rules are evaluated in order; the first failing rule determines the scene outcome (PRD section 3).

checks.reasoning: Fewer bands than the platform's expected band count
Scene extent smaller than 95% of the tasked AOI
Quality/cloud mask missing, unparseable, or covering less than the full scene footprint

rules.name: cloud_obstruction

checks.reasoning: Cloud/haze/smoke mask coverage exceeds the 40% usable threshold

rules.note: Re-task (not merely reprocess) when obstruction exceeds 80% — see PRD section 3 QA-3.

rules.name: sensor_artifact
rules.levels_note: The pixel_quality_mask (which QA-4 reads) is delivered on L2A products in this catalog (Wyvern's ODP publishes no L1B items — see data/README.md), so QA-4 applies at both L1B and L2A.

checks.reasoning: Dead/saturated (interpolated) pixel count exceeds 2% of total pixels
Any full-band dropout detected in the pixel quality mask
PRD §3: worst single red-edge band (711-782nm) exceeds the 0.1% ceiling — stricter than the scene-wide average because the PRD treats the red edge as the high-value range
Reflectance outside physical [0,1] bounds on more than 0.5% of valid (unmasked) pixels

Internally inconsistent reflectance: mean band-to-band correlation on clear pixels below the expected range for hyperspectral surface data (adjacent bands of a well-calibrated stack are strongly correlated) — the output contradicts its own inputs

PRD §3: worst spatial tile's band correlation falls below 0.5 — a localized inconsistency that a scene-wide average can dilute and miss; the tile threshold is looser than the scene-wide 0.7 because a single tile's smaller sample is naturally noisier
